texts.220g-P14pP15o:
“Nothing suppressed, everything processed” can be taken to mean that someone in the group must tell all, even if they don’t want to. I have seen that risk in groups that use the ZEGG Forum practice. A group starts out inviting honesty and ends up treating privacy as resistance.

Peer counseling can become peer surveillance, even if the tone is warm. And when things like that are required as pre-reqs for people to get medicine, it can give the gatekeepers power over people right when they are at their most open. Even something couched in words like “willing to be seen” could become a demand that people disclose whatever the group wants them to.

The boundary is simple. These aren't principles to give the community power over me, they're principles I choose to guide my own practice.
